title: Active and Creative Kids voucher – Privacy Collection Notice for providers
summary: This notice explains why and how Service NSW collects personal information from providers participating in the Active and Creative Kids voucher program.
intro:
This Privacy Collection Notice relates to the Active and Creative Kids voucher program.

The Active and Creative Kids Voucher Program (the Program) is being delivered by Service NSW and the Department of Customer Service on behalf of the NSW Government. The Program aims to support certain families with school-aged children to access sport and recreational and/or creative and cultural activities.
who_can_apply: Must be a provider participating in the Active and Creative Kids voucher program.
what_you_need: Proof of identity document (such as a driver's licence or Australian passport).
Business details for verification (e.g., through the Australian Business Register, ASIC, and NSW incorporated Associations Register).
Working With Children Check number and completion of the Child Safe eLearning Module.
Relevant swimming instructor accreditation information (if applicable).

more_info.text: Please see our privacy statement for more information about how Service NSW handles your personal information. This includes how you can access and seek correction of the information, how privacy enquiries or complaints can be made, how information is securely stored, and how to contact us. Service NSW is located at 2–24 Rawson Place Sydney NSW 2000.

faqs.q: What is the Active and Creative Kids voucher program?
faqs.a: The program supports families with school-aged children to access sport, recreational, and/or creative and cultural activities.

faqs.q: What information is collected from providers?
faqs.a: Information collected includes name, date of birth, email address, phone number, and details from a proof of identity document.

faqs.q: Who will receive the provider's personal information?
faqs.a: Information may be disclosed to the Department of Customer Service, public/private entities (like the Document Verification Service), the Australian Business Register, and other agencies for verification and compliance.
